$comment: Single machine home for WoW v2 formats. Consumed by gates.sh AND status.mjs. If docs/process/FORMATS.md disagrees with this file, this file wins and the disagreement is a defect. Nothing in gates.py or status.mjs may inline a pattern, a path or a vocabulary word that belongs here.

ids.$obligation_comment: F-55 (v0.7.2): the two-digit ceiling expired silently the day a pilot passed OBL-*-99 (they are at 134) — no id is parsed positionally, so the bound bought nothing. {2,} keeps the alignment minimum. The key now HAS a consumer: _gap_rows validates every OBL- row id against it, so the declaration can no longer be wrong and inert at once.
ids.$cv_short_comment: OBL-PKG-13 (v0.7.0): the shorthand CV-<nn> is legal INSIDE its own run's artifacts and resolves to the run's full id; every durable home (GAPS.md) carries the full form — it is the id that outlives the run. The escrow resolves shorthands and demands the full row; real reports write the short form (frisbii's CV-01..05 were invisible to the long regex).
ids.$run_parts_comment: Audit A1 (engine round 6): the anatomy is named parts so DIAGNOSTICS derive from the same source the gates match against — GATE-1's zero-hit diagnosis and check-id previously restated the date/slug/iter shape as inline literals, in the very release whose headline was 'the run id has ONE definition'. The slug CAP is never written anywhere else either: consumers derive it by probing run_slug (gates.py _slug_cap), so widening the cap here is the whole change.
ids.$task_tail_comment: F-39 (v0.7.1): the task-id tail is a template key like {run_core} — it was spelled twice (ids.task and the [T:] trailer), and two spellings of one grammar is the restatement class F-46 closed for the run id. Both engines expand {task_tail} at load.
ids.$run_core_comment: F-46/F-39 (v0.7.1): the run-id shape was restated in FOUR places (run, task, cannot_validate, the [T:] trailer) plus three branch patterns — a widening of one was a silent narrowing of another, which is exactly how a 27-char slug passed P0→G2 and then no executor commit could carry a legal lane ref. {run_core} is the single source; both engines expand it at load. Slug cap raised 24→48 — a PO-chosen headroom over the longest observed failing slug (27 chars, F-46), not a value derived from slug-length data; the pattern is anchored, so there is no backtracking argument for keeping it tight. The task tail admits an insertion suffix T<nn>[a-z] — task rows get inserted into signed plans without renumbering; the F-39 report cites T13b/T07a in pilot archives (pilot-reported, not independently verified here). Validate at run-open: gates.sh check-id <id> (P1) — the operator learns the cap before a spec is signed against the id, not at day three.

paths.$comment: Every repo-relative location the gates and status.mjs read. Inlining any of these in a consumer is the defect this section exists to prevent.

commit_trailers.$comment: GATE-1. Exactly one must appear in a commit message. Each names a lane whose path must exist AND resolve to a real record. The task pattern embeds ids.task so the trailer and the id can never drift apart.
commit_trailers.$strip_comment: git commit -v appends the diff below a scissors line. Counting trailers quoted in that diff produced false 'two lane references' rejections, so everything from the scissors line on is dropped before matching.

task.$comment: Derived from ids.run_core + the task tail — never restated (F-39: the restated two-digit tail meant _parse_plan admitted T07a while zero trailer kinds matched it, and the operator was told 'no lane reference' about a lane reference they had written).

migrate.$comment: review PR-4: migration commits (lifting durables from .planning into docs/) had no legal lane ref, training operators to fake [WOW:publish]. Valid ONLY mid-migration: .planning/ exists AND migrated_from_gsd is still false. Greenfield repos and post-freeze repos reject it.

run.$comment: F-08/F-10 (v0.6.3): P1 and P4 artifacts had no trailer that resolves — the spec a PO signs at G1 and the reconciled spec/divergence/RUN-REPORT at G4 sat outside git at the moment of signing, and the improvisation pressure (borrow a task id, fake a publish) is the class PR-4 existed to stop. The bare form [T:<run-id>] (no .Tnn suffix) resolves to the run DIRECTORY, which may exist before its plan. Phase-level artifacts of a run commit under it; task work still requires the fully-qualified form.

commit_trailers.$doc_literal_comment: PF-b: the literal an operator-facing doc must contain for this trailer to count as documented. Consumed by check_parity's reverse direction: every kind must appear in each of parity.lane_docs and one of parity.router_locations.

branch_patterns.$base_ref_comment: GATE-2 and GATE-5 use this to answer 'what did this run modify?': the diff from the run base to HEAD, plus the working tree. Absent base branch -> the run's own commits cannot be isolated and the modified set degrades to staged + unstaged changes.
branch_patterns.$main_comment: F-11 (v0.6.2): the refs gate-7 --p5 tries, in order, as the published branch the run must not be behind. Repo-local override: `main_branch` in wow.config.json. None resolving is a loud failure, not a skip.

status_vocab.$comment: FORMATS §4. No synonyms. evidence_required members need an ev: citation in the same row or sentence; reference_required members need either an ev: citation or one of reference_id_patterns (GATE-3).
status_vocab.$evidence_required_comment: FORMATS §4: COMPLETED (ev required) and FAILED (ev of failure). Gating only COMPLETED left half of §4's promise unenforced.
status_vocab.$done_words_comment: GATE-3. Used as a STATUS. Prose use is not gated; the check requires the word to head a table cell or follow a status colon.
status_vocab.$status_columns_comment: When a scanned table has a header row naming one of these, only that column is status-checked. Checking every cell made 'OK' and 'PASS' in a Done-means or Verify column read as forbidden synonyms. A table with no header row is still checked in full.
status_vocab.$verdict_comment: F-10 (v0.6.2): a STATUS describes the work (executor); a VERDICT is an independent judgement about it (verifier). P3 mandates the grade and GATE-3 was rejecting it — 56 hits in one run, 10 of them the mandated PASS. Where a table names a Grade/Verdict column, that column is checked against verdict_vocab instead of the status vocabulary; FAIL must carry a VF id and PASS-with-carry-forwards a CV id in the same row. COMPLETED+FAIL is the most important pair a run produces — collapsing them loses it.
status_vocab.$fail_comment: FAIL is a verdict, not a status (F-20): bare FAIL in a status column previously matched NO branch and passed in silence; it now trips the synonym check with a pointer at Grade/Verdict headers. FAILED remains the status.

claim_labels.$comment: FORMATS §2. CONVENTION, reviewed at gates, NOT gated. status.mjs reports density; gates.sh must never reject on these.

evidence.$comment: FORMATS §3. ENFORCED subset — GATE-3 requires one of these alongside an evidence-required status or a done-word, AND requires it to be well formed per types below.
evidence.$validate_shape_comment: GATE-3 once accepted ev:cmd{i ran it and it was fine} because only `any` was applied. A citation that cites nothing checkable satisfies the letter of the gate and defeats its purpose, so each occurrence is now matched against its own type pattern.
evidence.$file_line_comment: GATE-5 preflight target. Content anchors (path#anchor) are preferred and are not line-checked.
evidence.$braces_comment: frisbii braces finding (v0.6.2): the body admits ONE level of balanced braces, so awk action blocks, jq object construction and regex quantifiers are citable. Deeper nesting cannot be expressed: `opener` catches an ev: prefix the kind regex cannot parse, and the diagnostic says THE FORMAT cannot express it — never that the writer's citation is malformed for the wrong reason. Backticked citations are mentions (v0.6.1 PF-a) and are not scanned at all.
evidence.$attest_comment: F-27 (v0.6.3): evidence for a task placed with a human IS a person's decision — 'the operator read one row and declined to issue the next statement' has no command to cite, and dressing it as ev:cmd records a human decision in the grammar of a shell command. ev:attest{who: claim @date}. The opener is now GENERIC: an ev: token whose kind is outside evidence.types is a GATE-3 failure — a malformed known kind failed loudly while an invented kind was silently invisible, and the invented kind is the author who believes they are complying.

scan_targets.$comment: The document set GATE-3 and GATE-5 sweep. GATES-SPEC names these docs in prose; this is their machine home.

$citation_scan_exclude_comment: GATE-3 and GATE-5 skip these. Negative-test fixtures contain deliberately broken citations and deliberately wrong statuses — that is their job. Scanning them makes every commit fail, and a gate that cries wolf is a gate someone disables.

codebase_frontmatter.$comment: FORMATS §6, GATE-6. Freshness is git-only: fresh iff `git log <verified_against>..HEAD -- <paths>` is empty. No calendar component.

p0_record.$comment: The escape hatch GATE-6 honours when an area has no map: the ORCH records the P0 outcome in the run's HANDOFF. It is a format, so it lives here and is documented in FORMATS §6 — an engine-only vocabulary nobody can read is not an escape hatch, it is a trapdoor.

dep_frontmatter.$comment: FORMATS §11 (v0.4.1). External-dependency maps live in docs/deps/<name>.md — NOT docs/codebase/, because §6's git freshness rule is meaningless for a surface you do not version. Fresh iff the probe's current output hash equals verified_against_hash; where no probe surface is definable, fresh iff verified is within max_age_days. A changed hash does not mean the map is wrong — it means the vendor surface moved since verification, so re-verify.

freshness.$hash_comment: gates.sh hashes the probe's stdout. A probe that itself ends in a digest command still works — it hashes a hash, deterministically — but emitting the raw surface content is preferred, so verified_against_hash stays reproducible with a single tool.
freshness.$probe_trust_comment: The probe is a shell command read from a repo file and executed by the gate. That is the same trust level as a git hook or a Makefile target, and it is why --no-probe exists: freshness then degrades to the max_age_days fallback rather than silently passing.

dep_frontmatter.$probe_comment: frisbii S-2 (v0.6.2): a probe: line is executed as shell, so what it may BE is part of the schema. The first executable word must match this pattern (default: a repo-local script, i.e. the request wrapper) — checked BEFORE execution, failing loudly with NO fallback to the calendar branch (a rejected probe silently reporting fresh is the failure mode). Repo-local override: `probe_command_pattern` in wow.config.json, like requirement_id.

frontmatter.$comment: YAML front-matter subset the gates parse, shared by codebase and dependency maps.

plan_schema.$comment: GATE-8. PLAN.md must parse against this.
plan_schema.$inputs_comment: F-58 (v0.7.2): a unit's declared cross-unit inputs — paths it READS that another unit produces. GATE-8 checks each one is covered by some other unit's owns at a STRICTLY LOWER wave, or the input is unreachable by construction under the branch model (wave-N branches carry only waves <N). Undeclared inputs stay invisible; the field exists so the dependency is a lint, not an adversarial-review catch — eight plan revisions and seven review rounds missed one.
plan_schema.$columns_comment: GATE-8 locates Verify by header, not by position. Reading cell index 2 unconditionally let a plan that ordered its columns differently ship tasks with an empty Verify cell.
plan_schema.$areas_comment: FORMATS §6 plan linkage: a unit names the codebase areas it touches, so GATE-6(a) has a machine input instead of depending on the operator remembering --area.
plan_schema.$deps_comment: FORMATS §11 plan linkage: a unit names the external dependencies it relies on. GATE-6 requires a fresh docs/deps/<name>.md for each before the plan may proceed.
plan_schema.$task_verify_comment: Every auto task needs a verify command. A task whose Verify cell begins with MANUAL: is a manual check and must name an owner.
plan_schema.$spec_must_declare_acs_comment: A spec whose ACs are not table rows yielded an empty AC set, and 'every AC mapped' was then vacuously true. GATE-8 now fails when the spec declares no parseable AC at all.
plan_schema.$unit_body_end_comment: A unit's body ends at the next level-2 section. Without this the last unit swallowed the Coverage matrix, whose rows name task ids and were read as task rows.
plan_schema.$non_vacuity_comment: F-9 / GATE-13 (v0.6.2): one cell per task naming a plausible wrong answer the Verify rejects, citing something runnable (gate-4's proof rule), or MANUAL for a PO-owned row. Deliberately NOT in task_table_columns: GATE-8 must keep passing signed historical plans; GATE-13 owns the column and binds only while the plan is unsigned.
plan_schema.$contracts_comment: F-28 (v0.6.3): the unit section is the only channel to an executor (P3: manifest = unit section + interface contracts + CONVENTIONS, nothing else), so a rule that binds EVERY unit needs a home P3 delivers — a credential-safety prohibition written into an amendment section was gated, committed, and read by nobody. P3 appends '## Contracts' to every executor manifest; GATE-8 flags normative language outside unit sections and this block.

report_row_schema.$comment: RUN-REPORT.md location and required sections. F-14 (v0.6.3): this schema USED to carry a `row` regex whose comment claimed GATE-3 consumed it — no engine ever read it, and its digit-excluding status class contradicted status_vocab.cascade_form two keys away. An unread schema that looks authoritative is a third source of truth; deleted rather than wired, because GATE-3's real row handling (status_vocab) is the single home.

requirements_row_schema.$updated_comment: GATE-2 says 'updated technical-status row', not 'a row exists'. A REQ whose row predates the run and was never touched is exactly the phase-close failure the gate is for, so the row must appear in the run's diff.
requirements_row_schema.$row_comment: PF-d (pilot #2, v0.6.0): {req} is substituted with the EFFECTIVE requirement id pattern — wow.config.json `requirement_id` if set, else ids.requirement. A brownfield repo with stable non-REQ identities (e.g. PLAT-M3-nn) configures the pattern instead of renumbering or running a permanently-vacuous GATE-2. Rows whose first cell is id-shaped but unreadable by the effective pattern FAIL GATE-2 loudly (FR-1's rule applied here). Dual consumers: gates.py and status.mjs.
requirements_row_schema.$declaration_comment: F-17 (v0.6.4, frisbii): GATE-2's obligation set was a literal text scan, so a range (REQ-059 … REQ-063) enrolled two of five rows, and any scanned doc that DISCUSSED an id adopted it — a repo's own record of its gate defects was unwritable. When the spec header carries a 'requirements:' line or any unit declares 'governs:', those declarations ARE the set (mention ≠ claim — the move _governing_sources already made). With no declaration anywhere, the legacy scan applies, with an advisory nudge.

jira_mapping.$comment: FORMATS §10, GATE-10. Expected-consistent pairs. Out-of-mapping = divergence, classified never merged.
jira_mapping.$divergence_comment: gates.sh cannot call the Atlassian MCP. GATE-10 checks that the ORCH produced a divergence record for the gate, that every row carries a classification IN THE CLASSIFICATION COLUMN, that any pair it records is genuinely out of the expected mapping above, and that an empty diff is evidenced rather than asserted. Producing the diff is an MCP action; verifying it is complete is mechanical.
jira_mapping.$no_divergence_comment: A bare 'No divergences.' is a claim, not a diff. It carries an ev: citation of the MCP query that produced it — the same evidence rule every other completion claim obeys.

offline_deferral.$comment: GATES-SPEC: offline -> diff deferred to jira-queue AND the deferral recorded. A divergence record that says MCP was unavailable must be matched by an open jira-queue item, or the deferral is not recorded anywhere that will be chased.
offline_deferral.$claim_comment: How a divergence record says 'I could not reach Jira'. Saying it obliges an open jira-queue item; otherwise the deferral is recorded nowhere that will be chased.

jira_mapping.$signed_status_comment: Case-SENSITIVE and deliberately so. Matching case-insensitively made GATE-9 read the prose 'not signable, not signed' in a blocked draft's header as a sign-off claim. A gate that fires on prose is as useless as one that never fires.

closing_gates.$comment: GATE-9: which artifact governs which gate's closure. Passing --gate makes the record REQUIRED, not merely consistent; the sweep form stays a consistency lint because a sweep does not know what is closing.

jira_mapping.$signoff_gate_comment: F-15 (v0.6.3): the record may carry the gate it attests — 'signed: G4 2026-08-24 ev:jira{K-1}'. When present, gate-9 --gate G<n> requires it to MATCH: a G1 record on a superseded spec was closing G4. Legacy tokenless records remain valid (a date and a key), but new sign-offs should carry the token; the sweep lint accepts both.

non_vacuity.$comment: GATE-4. An invariant declares a rule; a non-vacuity proof shows the rule can fail. The proof must cite something runnable — an ev: citation or a path that exists — because 'non-vacuity: yes' is not a proof.
non_vacuity.$install_test_comment: Gate logic and gate WIRING are different claims. Every gate had a passing negative test while GATE-7 was absent from the sweep, GATE-6's area half had no caller, and hooks were installed where core.hooksPath meant git would never read them — because every test called gates.sh directly. test-install.sh commits through the real hooks after a real install.

runs_layout.$single_home_comment: ORCH-owned files live once, in plan_schema.orch_owned_paths. A basename copy here would be a second home for one fact inside the single-home file itself.
runs_layout.$findings_comment: audit-run verdict table (PO decision 2026-08-18, review FR-9): named so escrow/GC/archival know it is load-bearing
runs_layout.$handoff_comment: handoff_max_lines counts as wc -l does (frisbii off-by-one, v0.6.2: split-on-newline counted the trailing newline, so 80 meant 79 and no conforming file could reach the stated limit). The limit is ADVISORY by PO decision 2026-08-24 — status.mjs reports the overage; no gate acts on it.
runs_layout.$portable_comment: F-35 (v0.6.4): backslash-Z is Python end-of-string and a JavaScript literal 'Z' — one key, two engines, opposite answers (16 healthy quick notes reported stale to a PO for deletion). Shared regexes use the portable subset; the parity sweep refuses the backslash-Z and backslash-A escapes anywhere in this file (it caught this very comment spelling them out). $(?![\s\S]) is the portable end-of-input.

legacy_freeze.$comment: GATE-11. Inert unless wow.config.json sets the config key true. Frozen means frozen in every direction: additions, edits, renames AND deletions. Filtering deletions out of the staged set let `git rm -r .planning/` erase the history the gate exists to preserve.

gate_failure_recovery.$comment: FORMATS §7. status.mjs reports attempts against this; gates never bypass.

audit_triggers.$comment: P4. Counters derived by status.mjs; any hit schedules an audit phase before new feature work.

AT-1.$comment: F-47 (v0.7.2): the count EXCLUDES artifacts serving as non-vacuity controls — negative tests, mutants, planted violations, subject-absent probes. The framework DEMANDS those (GATE-13, the two-negative-tests rule), so a counter that reads them as mock drift fires hardest on the healthiest runs: two firings, zero audits, both waived (pilot #2). AT-1 is orch-recorded judgment; the recorded number is committed-mocks-and-fixtures-standing-in-for-real-systems, and a control that proves a check can fail is not one. F-40 (v0.7.1): counts artifacts that SURVIVE the run — committed under the repo, or referenced by something that is. A falsification audit's throwaway scratch fixtures are not fixtures the next run inherits, and the old bare count fired at 90x threshold on a run that added ZERO fixtures to the codebase — hardest on exactly the class of run the trigger most wants to encourage. Created-but-destroyed counts are reported in prose if worth noting; they are never the trigger.

AT-4.$source_comment: status.mjs does not re-implement the citation rule; it runs the gate that owns it and reads the count. One implementation, two consumers — which is the whole point of this file.

audit_triggers.$derived_by_comment: status = status.mjs computes it from the repo. orch = recorded by the orchestrator in RUN-REPORT; not derivable from files alone. po = a judgment call recorded at G4. AT-4 was previously annotated 'derived by gates.sh gate-5 sweep' while no such counter existed in the engine — status.mjs now derives it directly, using the same citation rules gates.sh applies.
audit_triggers.$orch_comment: F-33 (v0.6.4): derived_by 'orch' means READ IT FROM THE DURABLE HOME — the run's RUN-REPORT '## audit triggers' table (| AT-n | value | ...) — never 'give up'. Three of five triggers rendered 'not derived' against numbers that were derived, recorded and cited: PF-03's founding gap recurring in the file that fixed it. AT-5 is a genuine PO judgement and stays null, saying so.

install.$comment: INSTALL.md's machine half: what install.sh writes, and what --check compares. Listed here so the installer, --check and status.mjs cannot disagree about what a complete installation is.
install.$hook_marker_comment: --check greps for this marker AND diffs the body against the canonical hook. Grepping for the string 'gates.sh' reported ok for a hook someone had rewritten to `# gates.sh` + `exit 0`.
install.$preserved_hook_comment: A target repo's existing commit-msg/pre-commit hook is moved aside, not destroyed, and the WoW hook chains to it. Overwriting a project's lint hook to install ours is the kind of collateral damage that gets a framework uninstalled.

prerequisites.$comment: Documented in INSTALL.md and README.md. install.sh checks these before writing anything.

notes.bash: install.sh, gates.sh and the negative tests are bash scripts. macOS ships 3.2; nothing here needs bash 4.
notes.git: 2.5 introduced `git worktree` and --git-common-dir, which is how hooks reach every worktree.
notes.python3: gates.sh is a thin wrapper; gates.py is the engine. install.sh also uses python3 to rewrite the CLAUDE.md section in place.
notes.node: status.mjs only. Gates do not need node; a repo without node loses derived status, not enforcement.

install.$seed_comment: F-06 (v0.6.3): which commands THIS repo's verify steps may run is repo-local truth by definition (a k8s platform needs kubectl, a Java service gradle) — shipping it in engine_files meant --check reported the repo's own policy as DRIFTED and the next upgrade overwrote it (observed: 18 designed vs 234 accreted, overlap zero). Seeded once from the package template, then owned by the repo, like wow.config.json; --check reports MISSING but never drift.

covers: external-dep freshness (FORMATS §11, probe-hash rule, max_age_days fallback)

GATE-12.$comment: Not in the sweep lists: it needs invocation context (--kind). The P1 command stub runs it; test-gate-12.sh proves the logic, test-install proves the stub names it.

GATE-13.$comment: F-9: plan Verify non-vacuity. Unsigned plans only — a signed plan is frozen and a retroactive rule would demand the edit the framework prohibits. The pilot implemented this as its local GATE-12 at v0.5.1; upstream the id 12 was already the obligation block, so it lands as GATE-13.

GATE-14.$comment: PII scan — see pii_scan. Non-vacuity: a staged capture with a populated email must be refused; the same file with the field emptied, or carrying 'pii-ok: <reason>', must not.

sweep.$comment: GATES-SPEC: full sweep at every gate + P5. GATE-7 is a P5 check (a mid-run jira-queue legitimately has open items), so it joins the sweep only under --p5. Leaving it out of every sweep list meant a gate with a passing negative test that nothing ever called.

gap_row.$comment: FORMATS 12: docs/GAPS.md is the obligation registry. Consumed by gate_12, gate_7's escrow check, and status.mjs. A row is OPEN unless its id cell is struck through (~~OBL-XXX-01~~ = discharged; the discharge ev: citation joins the ev cell). The effect enum is CLOSED: an unrecognized value fails validation loudly and is never treated as non-blocking (v0.5.6, pilot N3).
gap_row.$spec_kinds_comment: gate-12 --kind: 'feature' is refused while a blocks-new-feature-work row is open; audit/fix/probe are the discharge paths and must --ref the open obligation they discharge. 'remediation' (F-53, v0.7.2) is the category for repairing a defect a prior run shipped: it discharges no blocker, so its --ref must resolve to a RECORDED DEFECT (PARK/VF/DEF-plan/CV id, or a registry row) somewhere in runs/ or the registry — the same shape of proof, pointed at the thing that justifies the work. New capability under a remediation flag is a G1 review refusal, not a mechanical one.
gap_row.$scope_comment: stops at whitespace OR ')': '(scope: *)' is scope '*', not '*)' — the greedy \S+ let a planted blocks-install row slip past the installer in the wiring test
gap_row.$row_start_comment: matches ANY letter-prefixed id-shaped first cell (OBL-, CV-, G-, REQ-...), not only OBL-: a registry whose rows the schema cannot read must fail LOUDLY, never parse as empty (review FR-1 — frisbii's 5-column G-nn table read as an empty registry and gate-12 went green-because-empty)

parity.$comment: verifier F5: check_parity's doc set and spec locations were inline literals in gates.py — the function enforcing layer parity was itself the violator. Single home restored.
parity.$reverse_comment: PF-b (pilot #2, v0.6.0): check_parity was one-directional — engine-ahead-of-docs was invisible ([WOW:migrate] absent from LANES.md and the router). lane_docs must each document every commit-trailer kind's doc_literal; router_locations is a fallback list (package repo uses CLAUDE-WOW-SECTION.md, installed repos the CLAUDE.md wow section).

verify_lint.$comment: F-9 (v0.6.2): five idioms that each shipped a real inert Verify in pilot #1's run 260821-frisbii-ops-r1. A match is a GATE-13 failure unless the row carries the accept marker with a reason — accepting one deliberately and VISIBLY. A lint cannot catch the next vacuous idiom; that is what the Non-vacuity column is for. Python-regex flavor; consumed by gates.py only.

pii_scan.$comment: frisbii PII composition (v0.6.4): capture-whole + widened scope committed 159 third-party customer records with every gate green — the framework had a rule about what must be captured and none about what may be committed. GATE-14 scans STAGED files under a run's evidence path for populated personal-data field names. Heuristic by design; the escape marker makes a deliberate capture possible and VISIBLE, and P3's declared-trim convention keeps the scrubbed capture honest.

feedback.$comment: FORMATS §13. F-37 (v0.6.4): the log kept pace and the write-up doc did not, twice, with the first occurrence predicting the second. gate-7 --p5 reconciles them — ONLY when the log exists, so repos without a feedback log carry no burden. A logged F-nn owes a write-up (an 'F-nn' heading or a findings/F-nn.md) under the upstream dir before publish.
